mainTopic: The final part of the משנה's dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a woman who saw blood on the eleventh day of her ימי זיבה and then immersed and had relations with her husband, plus related cases.
overview: The amud finishes the משנה about a woman who saw blood during her eleven ימי זיבה and then immersed and had relations too early. If she saw on the eleventh day and immersed that evening, בית הלל exempt the couple from a קרבן. If she immersed on the twelfth day and then saw blood, בית שמאי say she makes משכב and מושב טמא but there is no קרבן. בית הלל agree that seeing inside the eleven days and immersing that evening brings full טומאה and a קרבן. Immersing on the clean day itself is called תרבות רעה, and everything stays on hold. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that narrows the dispute to the eleventh day alone. It then records a sharp debate in which בית שמאי demand 'השוו מדותיכם' and בית הלל answer that a precaution works 'to be strict, not lenient', a principle בית שמאי themselves use. Next, רב הונא says בית שמאי make her משכב and מושב טמא on the second day even if she saw no more blood. רב יוסף, רב כהנא and אביי debate whether the משנה already teaches this. אביי raises difficulties against רב הונא, ending with a משנה from זבים, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית הלל exempt the couple from a קרבן in the eleventh-day case
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל finish the dispute from the case just before: the couple who had relations after she saw on the eleventh day and immersed that evening do not bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: They are exempt from the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is completing an argument that started just before this section. בית שמאי had said the couple must bring a קרבן, and now בית הלל say they are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who saw blood on day eleven, the last of the ימי זיבה, then immersed that evening and had relations without waiting a clean day. בית הלל exempt them from a קרבן because day twelve is not a day that can make her a זבה. So she did not truly need to wait a clean day after day eleven.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from bringing the sin offering
The eleven days between נדה periods, when bleeding can make a woman a זבה
The eleventh day, which is the last of the ימי זיבה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a brand-new case. It is the second half of a dispute about the eleventh-day case, which starts just before this section.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
They are exempt from the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: פְּטוּרִים מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute that began in the lines just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, a couple who had relations after she saw on day eleven and immersed that evening are exempt from a קרבן.

steps.title: Immersing on the twelfth day and then seeing blood: בית שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: In a new case, she immerses on the twelfth day, has relations, and then sees blood. בית שמאי say she makes משכב and מושב טמא, but there is no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she immersed on the day after day eleven (the twelfth day), had relations with her husband, and afterward saw blood, בית שמאי say: they make items for lying and sitting טמא, and they are exempt from the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case. This time she immerses during the twelfth day instead of waiting until it ends, and then she sees blood after relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי give a split ruling. On the טומאה side, they treat her as able to make what she lies or sits on טמא. On the קרבן side, they exempt the couple, because blood seen on day twelve cannot join day eleven to make her a real זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: She immersed on the following day, during the day rather than after it ended
She had relations with her husband (literally, 'served her household')
Items made for lying and sitting, which a זבה makes טמא

phrases.english: If she immersed on the day after it,
phrases.notes: 'The day after' means the twelfth day, right after the eleventh day when she saw blood.

phrases.english: and had relations with her husband,
and afterward she saw blood —
Beit Shammai say:
They make items for lying and sitting impure,
and they are exempt from the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבְלָה בַּיּוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו, וְשִׁמְּשָׁה אֶת בֵּיתָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new case that builds on the eleventh-day scenario.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: she makes משכב and מושב טמא, but the couple brings no קרבן.

steps.title: בית הלל call the husband a glutton
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל respond to the twelfth-day case by criticizing the husband as a גרגרן for not waiting, without declaring any טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: This man is a glutton.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give their view on the twelfth-day case. Instead of ruling טומאה, they just criticize the husband's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling him a גרגרן means he could not hold back until the twelfth day was over. They disapprove of the timing, but they do not say she makes משכב and מושב טמא the way בית שמאי did.

keyTerms.meaning: A glutton, someone who cannot hold back his desires

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל's criticism is not a ruling of טומאה. They disapprove of what he did, but they do not declare impurity.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
This one is a glutton,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the husband, who couldn't wait until the end of the twelfth day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: הֲרֵי זֶה גַּרְגְּרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's opposing view on the case from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: in the twelfth-day case the behavior is improper, but no טומאה is decreed.

steps.title: בית הלל agree when she sees inside the eleven days and immerses that evening
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל agree with בית שמאי that if she saw blood inside the eleven days and immersed that same evening, there is full טומאה and a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if she sees blood within the eleven days, then immerses that evening and has relations, they make items for lying and sitting טמא, and they are obligated to bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where בית הלל agree with בית שמאי. This is a case of bleeding in the middle of the eleven days, not on the last day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she sees inside the eleven days, the next day is still one of the ימי זיבה, so she must wait a clean day (שומרת יום כנגד יום). If she immerses that same evening, the immersion does not help her. So everyone agrees she makes things טמא and the couple must bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree; here, בית הלל agree with בית שמאי
Within the eleven ימי זיבה, before the last day
A woman who must wait one clean day for each day she saw blood
Obligated to bring a sin offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This line shows that בית הלל's leniency only applies because day eleven is the last day. Inside the eleven days, everyone agrees there is a קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדִים בְּרוֹאָה בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם,
phrases.english: And they agree regarding one who sees within the eleven days,
phrases.notes: 'They' is בית הלל agreeing with בית שמאי. 'Within' means before day eleven, so the next day still counts.

phrases.english: and immersed that evening and had relations —
that they make items for lying and sitting impure,
and they are obligated to bring an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים בְּרוֹאָה בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of בית הלל's leniency by naming a case where they agree with בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree: if she saw inside the eleven days and immersed that evening, there is טומאת משכב ומושב and a קרבן.

steps.title: Immersing the next day is bad practice, and everything is left hanging
steps.stepSummary: If she saw inside the eleven days and immersed the next day before it ended, then had relations, this is תרבות רעה. The status of what she touched and of their relations depends on what happens later.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she immersed on the following day and had relations, this is bad practice, and the status of what they touched and of their relations is left hanging.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a final case. She saw inside the eleven days, then immersed during the next day and had relations right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing partway through the clean day can work, but only if she does not see blood again that day. If she does see, the earlier immersion is cancelled, the items she touched become טמא, and the couple must bring a קרבן. Because they took that risk, the משנה calls it תרבות רעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bad practice; risky behavior that should be avoided
The items they touched
Their relations
Hanging, undecided until we see what happens

steps.whatToRemember: There are three key cases. Seeing on day eleven and immersing that evening: בית הלל exempt the couple from a קרבן. Seeing inside the eleven days and immersing that evening: everyone agrees on טומאה and a קרבן. Seeing inside the eleven days and immersing the next day: this is תרבות רעה, and everything depends on whether she sees blood again that day.

phrases.english: If she immersed on the day after it and had relations —
this is bad practice,
and what they touched and their relations are left hanging.
phrases.notes: If she sees blood later that day, it all becomes טמא and they owe a קרבן. If she doesn't, everything is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבְלָה בַּיּוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו, וְשִׁמְּשָׁה — הֲרֵי זֶה תַּרְבּוּת רָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the case of seeing inside the eleven days, now with immersion on the next day instead of that evening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing on the clean day itself and then having relations is improper, and the טהרות and the חיוב קרבן stay undecided until we know whether she sees blood that day.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists what both sides agree on
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says בית שמאי and בית הלל agree on two points. First, a זבה's night immersion does not count. Second, if she saw blood within the eleven days, immersed that evening, and had relations, she makes משכב and מושב טמא and they bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Both sides agree that when a זבה immerses at night, it is not a real immersion. They also agree about a woman who saw blood during the eleven days, immersed that same evening, and had relations. She makes lying and sitting places impure, and they must bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that first marks off the cases where there is no argument. This sets up the next line, which pins down exactly where they do argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who sees blood in the eleven days must wait one clean day and only then immerse, during the day. If she immerses that same night, the immersion is worthless, so she is still fully טמאה. This matches what the משנה already said in Step 4, and it gives us the baseline for the eleventh-day dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersing at night, which does not work for a זבה
A woman who saw blood outside her regular נדה time, during the eleven days
The eleven-day window after the נדה days, when blood makes her a זבה
Things made for lying or sitting on, which become טמא from her
They must bring a sin offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "within the eleven days" with "on the eleventh day." Both sides agree about the first. Only the second is argued about in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
And they agree about a night immersion for a zava
that it is not a valid immersion.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁוִין בְּרוֹאָה בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם
phrases.english: And they agree about one who sees blood within the eleven days
and immersed that evening and had relations
that she makes lying and sitting places impure,
and they are obligated to bring an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְשָׁוִין בִּטְבִילַת לַיְלָה לְזָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a ברייתא that restates and expands the agreed cases from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זבה's night immersion is invalid. Seeing within the eleven days and then immersing that night and having relations brings full טומאה and a קרבן, according to both sides.

steps.title: The only argument is about the eleventh day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says they argue only when she sees on the eleventh day itself. בית שמאי give full טומאה and a קרבן. בית הלל exempt from the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argued only about the eleventh day. בית שמאי say: they make lying and sitting places impure and must bring a קרבן. בית הלל exempt them from the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now names the one case in dispute: blood seen on the last day of the eleven, then immersion that evening and relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי treat the eleventh day exactly like any other day in the eleven. בית הלל break from them only on the קרבן. Notice that בית הלל do not argue about the משכב and מושב טומאה here.

keyTerms.meaning: They argued only about..., which narrows the dispute
The eleventh day itself, the last day of the זיבה window
Exempt

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם,
phrases.english: They disagreed only about the eleventh day,
for Beit Shammai say:
they make lying and sitting places impure
and are obligated to bring an offering,
and Beit Hillel exempt them from an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute down to the one case left after the agreed cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the eleventh day, בית שמאי require a קרבן and בית הלל exempt from it.

steps.title: בית שמאי ask why the eleventh day should be different
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי challenge בית הלל: you treat the eleventh day like the other days for טומאה, so why not for the קרבן too?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to בית הלל: What is the difference between the eleventh day and a day inside the eleven? If you make it equal for טומאה, shouldn't it be equal for the קרבן too?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי attack בית הלל's position as inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their logic: בית הלל already agree the eleventh day brings טומאה like the other days. So the eleventh day really is a day of זיבה, and the same result should follow for the קרבן. Splitting the two seems arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A challenge asking for a reason to split two cases
Made it equal, treated it the same
Ritual impurity

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
What is different about the eleventh day
from a day within the eleven?
If it was made equal to it for impurity,
should it not be equal to it for the offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא יוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר מִיּוֹם תּוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית הלל's exemption from the קרבן in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's exemption from a קרבן on the eleventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the eleventh day matches the other days for טומאה, it should also match them for the קרבן.

steps.title: בית הלל answer that the next day cannot join the eleventh
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reply that a day inside the eleven is stronger, because the following day can join with it toward זיבה. After the eleventh day, the next day cannot join, so the eleventh day is weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: No. You can say this about a day within the eleven, because the day after it joins with it to count toward זיבה. But can you say it about the eleventh day, when the day after it does not join with it toward זיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer the challenge by pointing to a real difference between the eleventh day and the earlier days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on an earlier day can link up with blood on the next day and build toward a bigger זיבה. The day after the eleventh is outside the זיבה window, so nothing can link with the eleventh day. That weakness is בית הלל's reason not to require a קרבן, even though they treat it the same for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: No, if you say..., an opening that rejects a comparison by showing a difference
Joins together, combines in the count
The state of being a זבה, counted by days of seeing blood

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: a day inside the eleven can join with the next day toward זיבה, but the eleventh day cannot. So on the eleventh day there is no קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם,
phrases.english: No. If you said this about within the eleven days,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן יוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו מִצְטָרֵף עִמּוֹ לְזִיבָה,
phrases.english: that is because the day after it joins with it toward ziva,
will you say it about the eleventh day,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין יוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו מִצְטָרֵף עִמּוֹ לְזִיבָה?!
phrases.english: when the day after it does not join with it toward ziva?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's challenge from Step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eleventh day is just like any day within the eleven, so it should require a קרבן too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eleventh day is weaker because the following day cannot combine with it toward זיבה, so it does not bring a קרבן.

steps.title: בית שמאי demand that בית הלל be consistent
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that if the eleventh day counts like the other days for טומאה, it must also count for the קרבן. If not for the קרבן, then not for טומאה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Be consistent! If you treat it the same for טומאה, treat it the same for the קרבן. And if you do not treat it the same for the קרבן, do not treat it the same for טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי attack בית הלל's position as inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said that seeing on the eleventh day makes things טמא like any other day, but there is no קרבן. בית שמאי say you cannot split the case: either it counts like the other days for everything, or it counts for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Make your measures equal, meaning be consistent in your rulings
Ritual impurity
Offering brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
Make your measures equal!
If you made it equal for impurity,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the eleventh day, made equal to the other days of זיבה.

phrases.english: make it equal for the offering;
and if you did not make it equal for the offering,
do not make it equal for impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues the debate with בית שמאי's demand for consistency.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's split ruling: טומאה yes, קרבן no, for seeing on the eleventh day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One case cannot be treated like the other days for one law and unlike them for the other law.

steps.title: Strict for טומאה does not mean requiring a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that making her טמא is a stringency, while requiring a קרבן would be a leniency, so the two do not have to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: Even if we brought it to טומאה, to be strict, we will not bring it to a קרבן, to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their split ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling her טמא only adds caution. Requiring a קרבן that may not truly be needed would mean bringing an animal that is not holy into the עזרה, which is a problem, so here the קרבן is the 'lenient' side. Being strict on both fronts means טומאה yes, קרבן no.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict
To be lenient
Into a state of, to the point of

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds odd to call a קרבן 'lenient'. The point is that bringing an offering that is not required is itself a problem, so requiring one is not the safe choice here.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
If we brought it to impurity, to be stringent,
we will not bring it to an offering, to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: אִם הֲבֵיאנוּהוּ לִידֵי טוּמְאָה לְהַחֲמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's demand for consistency.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle: be strict in both directions, not uniform in both laws.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Consistency means treating the case the same for טומאה and קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Consistency means always taking the stricter side: טומאה yes, קרבן no.

steps.title: בית הלל show that בית שמאי split the same way
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל point out that בית שמאי themselves say that a woman who immersed on the following day, had relations, and then saw again is טמא for משכב and מושב but exempt from a קרבן. So the same 'be consistent' challenge works against them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, you are bitten by your own words. You say: if she immersed on the following day, had relations, and afterward saw, she makes משכב and מושב טמא but is exempt from the קרבן. You too, be consistent: if you treat it the same for טומאה, treat it the same for the קרבן. And if you do not treat it the same for the קרבן, do not treat it the same for טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל turn בית שמאי's own argument back against them, using a ruling בית שמאי already accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בית שמאי's own case, the woman counts as a זבה for טומאה but not for a קרבן. That is the exact split בית שמאי just called inconsistent, so they cannot reject it in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitten, meaning refuted by your own words
She immersed in a מקוה
Items she lies or sits on, which become טמא
Exempt

phrases.english: And furthermore, from your own words you are bitten,
phrases.notes: A picture-phrase: your own statement 'bites' you, meaning it disproves you.

phrases.english: for you say:
if she immersed on the following day and had relations,
and afterward she saw blood,
she makes items for lying and sitting impure,
and she is exempt from the offering.
You too, make your measures equal:

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁיוָה לוֹ לַטּוּמְאָה, יִשְׁוֶה לוֹ לַקׇּרְבָּן.
phrases.english: if you made it equal for impurity, make it equal for the offering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא שָׁיוָה לוֹ לְקׇרְבָּן, לֹא יִשְׁוֶה לוֹ לַטּוּמְאָה!
phrases.english: And if you did not make it equal for the offering, do not make it equal for impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending themselves, בית הלל go on the attack using בית שמאי's own ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's demand that טומאה and קרבן always match.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי's own ruling has טומאה without a קרבן, so their own principle contradicts them.

steps.title: Strict, but not lenient: the same here
steps.stepSummary: Since בית שמאי must agree that their own case means 'strict but not lenient', the same principle applies to seeing on the eleventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say: to be strict and not to be lenient. Here too: to be strict and not to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל close the argument by stating the shared principle that explains both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's own split ruling only makes sense as 'be strict, not lenient'. Once they accept that, בית הלל's ruling on the eleventh day follows the same rule, and the charge of inconsistency falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, you must admit that
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's principle: when the רבנן extend טומאה to a case as a precaution, that extension works only to be strict. It does not create a חיוב קרבן, because an unneeded קרבן is not the safe side. בית שמאי already accept this principle in their own ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to be stringent and not to be lenient;
phrases.notes: This is how בית הלל explain בית שמאי's own ruling: equal only where that makes it stricter.

phrases.english: here too, to be stringent and not to be lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the counter-challenge in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both houses must accept 'strict, not lenient', so בית הלל's split ruling on the eleventh day is consistent.

steps.title: רב הונא: her bed and seat on the second day are impure even without new blood
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that בית שמאי make a woman's משכב and מושב on the second day טמא, even if she immersed and saw nothing more, because seeing blood that day would have made her טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Her bed and her seat on the second day, בית שמאי make them impure, even though she immersed, and even though she did not see blood. What is the reason? Since if she did see blood she would make them impure, now too she makes them impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a new ruling about בית שמאי's view. A woman who must wait one clean day immersed on that day, and בית שמאי still treat the bed and seat she used that day as טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She saw blood on one of her eleven days, so she must watch the next day to see if it stays clean. She immersed during that second day and saw nothing, yet בית שמאי still call her משכב and מושב טמא. The reason given is that the day is not yet safe: if she saw blood on it, it would make them טמא, so even now it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Her bed, or anything made for lying on, which she can make טמא
Her seat, or anything made for sitting on
Of the second day, the day after she saw blood
They declare it impure
Since, if it were the case that...

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מִשְׁכָּבָהּ וּמוֹשָׁבָהּ שֶׁבַּשֵּׁנִי,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Her bed and her seat on the second day,
phrases.notes: The second day is the day after she saw blood during her eleven days, the day she must watch to see if it stays clean.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai render them impure,
even though she immersed,
even though she did not see blood.
What is the reason?
Since if she were to see blood, she would make them impure,
now too she makes them impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate between the houses ends, a new statement explains בית שמאי's view in a case where she saw no more blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the משכב and מושב of the second day are טמא even if she immersed and did not see again, because seeing on that day would have made them טמא.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what רב הונא adds, since the משנה already says that בית שמאי make her משכב and מושב טמא when she immersed on the following day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is he teaching us? We already learned it: She immersed on the day after, had relations with her husband, and then saw blood. בית שמאי say: She makes beds and seats impure, and she is exempt from the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב הונא by asking what his statement adds. He quotes the משנה from step 2, which seems to teach the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, she immersed on the day after the eleventh day, and בית שמאי still say she makes משכב and מושב טמא. רב יוסף thinks that is the same idea as רב הונא's ruling, so רב הונא seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? A challenge that a statement adds nothing new
The day after (here, the day after the eleventh day)
She had relations with her husband
Exempt from bringing the offering

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is he teaching us?
We already learned: If she immersed on the following day,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה case from step 2, where she immersed on the day after the eleventh day.

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁמְּשָׁה אֶת בֵּיתָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאֲתָה —
phrases.english: and had relations with her husband, and afterward saw blood —
Beit Shammai say:
She makes beds and seats impure,
and she is exempt from the offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's statement as already taught in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב הונא's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already shows that בית שמאי make her משכב and מושב טמא even after she immersed on the following day, so רב הונא's ruling is not new.

steps.title: רב כהנא: in the משנה she saw blood
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא defends רב הונא: the משנה's case is different because she saw blood, while רב הונא teaches that she is טמא even with no new blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: When she saw blood, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב יוסף's challenge. He says the משנה only speaks about a woman who saw blood, so רב הונא is adding something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה alone, we might think בית שמאי make her טמא only because she saw blood afterward. רב הונא teaches that she is טמא even if she saw nothing at all, and that is his new point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different, so the case cannot be compared
She saw (blood)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: When she saw blood, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by pointing to a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might mean she is טמא only because she saw blood after immersing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא teaches that בית שמאי make her טמא even with no new blood.

steps.title: רב יוסף: seeing on that day is only a נדה sighting
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects רב כהנא's answer: blood seen on the twelfth day is a נדה sighting, not part of the זיבה count, so the משנה's case is the same as not seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And if she saw blood, what of it? It is a sighting of a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back against רב כהנא. He says the blood in the משנה does not change anything, so the משנה's case really is like רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's blood came on the day after the eleventh day, which already begins a new נדה period. Blood then is a נדה sighting and does not count toward זיבה. So the blood is not why she is טמא for משכב and מושב, and the משנה already covers a case with no relevant new blood.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? It makes no difference
A נדה sighting, blood that falls in the נדה period and not the זיבה days

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף holds that the משנה already teaches רב הונא's ruling, because blood on the twelfth day is only a נדה sighting and does not count toward זיבה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the blood in the משנה is what makes her טמא for משכב and מושב. רב יוסף's point is that this blood belongs to a new נדה period and has nothing to do with זיבה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וְכִי רָאֲתָה, מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: And if she saw blood, what of it?
It is a sighting of a menstruating woman!
phrases.notes: The twelfth day starts a new נדה period, so this blood does not count toward the eleven days of זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וְכִי רָאֲתָה, מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's way of telling the two cases apart.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב כהנא's claim that the משנה is different because she saw blood
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The blood seen on the twelfth day is a נדה sighting and does not affect זיבה, so it is the same as not seeing at all.

steps.title: אביי explains what was really bothering רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that רב כהנא was really asking a question. A decree makes sense when she saw blood, but when she saw nothing, what is there to decree?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: this is what bothered רב כהנא. When she did see blood, we understand the decree: we treat a נדה sighting strictly because it could be mixed up with a זבה sighting. But when she did not see anything at all, what decree could apply to her?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's rejection by retelling רב כהנא's point. רב כהנא was not just defending רב הונא; he was raising a difficulty against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that seeing on the twelfth day is a נדה sighting, so it is like not seeing at all. אביי says there is still a difference. A real sighting, even of נדה blood, can be decreed טמא because it looks like a זבה sighting. With no sighting at all there is nothing to attach a decree to, so רב הונא's ruling is hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (one case is fine, but...)
We make a rabbinic decree
Because of / on account of (being mixed up with)
A sighting of blood during the נדה period
A sighting of blood during the זיבה period

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רב יוסף said 'saw on day twelve' and 'didn't see' are the same. אביי says they are different: a real sighting can carry a decree, while no sighting cannot.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: This is what was difficult for Rav Kahana —
It makes sense where she saw blood,
we decree about a sighting of a נדה
because of a sighting of a זבה,
but where she did not see blood,
what should we decree about her?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's rejection in step 17 by showing that רב כהנא's distinction still holds, though as a difficulty against רב הונא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף thought seeing on the twelfth day and not seeing at all are the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A real sighting can be decreed טמא because it looks like a זבה sighting; with no sighting there is nothing to decree.

steps.title: A further challenge from the משנה in זבים
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה in which בית שמאי treat a man after one sighting of זוב like a שומרת יום כנגד יום. That sounds like a waiting status, which challenges רב הונא's claim that בית שמאי rule her definitely טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned: if someone sees one sighting of זוב, בית שמאי say he is like a woman who watches one clean day for one day of discharge. בית הלל say he is like a בעל קרי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second problem with רב הונא by quoting a משנה from זבים. In it, בית שמאי give the person a waiting status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יום כנגד יום immerses and then waits. If she sees nothing more, she stays טהור, and her status is only 'on hold.' If בית שמאי treat the day after one sighting this way, it is hard to see how they could make her משכב and מושב definitely טמא when no more blood came, as רב הונא said. בית הלל are more lenient: like a בעל קרי, his immersion makes him טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (adding another argument)
An unusual discharge that can make a person a זב or זבה
A woman who must watch one clean day after a day of seeing; her status hangs on that day
A man who had a seminal emission; immersion makes him טהור

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage. The גמרא will have to explain how רב הונא's reading of בית שמאי fits with this משנה.

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in זבים 1:1.

phrases.english: One who sees one sighting of זוב —
Beit Shammai say:
he is like a woman who watches a day for a day,
phrases.notes: His status is on hold: if he sees again that day, things he touched become טמא after the fact.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: like one who had an emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, source-based difficulty against רב הונא, on top of the logic-based difficulty in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement in step 14 that בית שמאי make her משכב and מושב טמא even when she saw nothing more
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי call the day after one sighting 'like a שומרת יום כנגד יום,' which is a suspended status. That does not fit definite טומאה when no further blood was seen.
